instructions.content: Choose the folder by what the artifact is (its typology), not by how long it lives
Keep one typology per file; NEVER merge a finding with a plan
The generator MUST own the filename and frontmatter; never hand-craft them
Extend the typology set deliberately, not per task
Choose the typology from the curated set; if none fits and the need will not recur, reuse the closest match instead of adding a folder
Inspect what already exists for the typology (for example ls .context/findings/) to avoid duplicates
Run the generator with a specific, task-tied title and verify the printed path uses the expected typology plus date
Fill in the body beneath the generated heading; if the content spans two typologies, split it into separate files
NEVER create a file without checking the typology folder first
NEVER use a generic slug like notes or todo
NEVER mix typologies in one file
NEVER hand-edit the filename or frontmatter date
NEVER emit related: [], blocks: [] or blocked-by: [] when there is nothing to list; omit the key
NEVER set blocked-by on a file whose blocker is unlikely to ever reach status: done
NEVER invent a new typology for a one-off; reuse the closest typology or pass --allow-new-type knowingly
Link files with --related, and record dependencies with --blocks on the depended-on file and --blocked-by on the depending file
Preview a file without writing it using --dry-run
Do not use the skill for inline code notes (code comment), permanent docs (README or docs site), issue tracking (issue tracker) or externally consumed content (docs system)
